clips.text: Hello! This is pixelreel. It turns a short list of scenes into a little narrated video, drawn in pixel art, that plays in any web browser. This one explains itself.
A reel is just a list of scenes. Each scene has four parts. A title. A caption, for reading along. The words the narrator says. And a picture.
Every picture is a small piece of code that draws on a grid of three hundred and twenty by one hundred and eighty chunky pixels. It knows how long the scene has been playing, so things can move.
The voice you are hearing was recorded ahead of time, on an ordinary computer, by Kokoro, an open speech model. One command records every scene. Change a line, and only that scene is recorded again.
No recording yet? That is fine. The browser reads the words aloud with its own built in voice, so a brand new reel plays straight away, while you are still writing it.
Watch it your way. Play, pause, go back, or skip ahead. Turn the sound off and read at your own pace. On a keyboard, the space bar plays and pauses, and the arrow keys move between scenes.
A reel is just a handful of plain files. No server code, and no accounts. Put them on GitHub Pages, or any other web host, and send someone the link.
Making your own takes three steps. Start a new reel with one command. Write your scenes. Then record the voices. That is all. Thanks for watching!
